name: A reported value is interpreted incorrectly because its number base is not stated
description: Values such as offsets, sector numbers and identifiers may be expressed in decimal or hexadecimal. A value containing only the digits 0-9 is valid in both bases, so a reader who assumes the wrong base derives a different number and may examine the wrong location or fail to match two references to the same item. Interpretation here means determining what a reported number denotes, not evaluative interpretation of findings.

references.relevance_summary_280: Provides an example showing that a value can be read as either decimal or hexadecimal, and argues that the number base must be reported with the value.
